title: The emergency oral Schedule II record, and what voids the authority to dispense
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1306.11(d)(2) the emergency oral Schedule II prescription SHALL BE IMMEDIATELY REDUCED TO WRITING BY THE PHARMACIST and shall contain all information 21 CFR 1306.05 requires EXCEPT the prescribing individual practitioner's signature. Under 1306.11(d)(4) the follow-up prescription must bear on its face 'AUTHORIZATION FOR EMERGENCY DISPENSING' AND THE DATE OF THE ORAL ORDER; it may be delivered in person or by mail, but a mailed paper prescription MUST BE POSTMARKED WITHIN THE 7-DAY PERIOD; UPON RECEIPT the dispensing pharmacist MUST ATTACH the paper prescription to the oral emergency prescription earlier reduced to writing, and for an ELECTRONIC follow-up must ANNOTATE the electronic prescription record with the original authorization and the date of the oral order. FAILURE OF THE PHARMACIST to notify the nearest DEA office when the practitioner does not deliver the follow-up SHALL VOID THE AUTHORITY conferred by 1306.11(d) to dispense without a written prescription. Under 1306.11(d)(5) a central fill pharmacy is not authorized to prepare a Schedule II prescription on an oral authorization from a retail pharmacist or practitioner.
exam_relevance: Tests the record layer of the emergency oral pathway and, in particular, that the pharmacist's own failure to notify the DEA retroactively removes the authority the emergency exception supplied.

authority.name: Emergency oral Schedule II records and follow-up handling

exceptions: A mailed follow-up satisfies the period by its postmark, not by the date the pharmacy receives it.
An electronic follow-up is annotated rather than physically attached.
The central fill prohibition in 1306.11(d)(5) removes the emergency oral route entirely for that setting.
common_confusions: Knowing the DEA notification duty without knowing that omitting it voids the authority to have dispensed at all.
Treating 'Authorization for Emergency Dispensing' as the whole face requirement and omitting the date of the oral order.
Reading the reduce-to-writing duty as optional because the emergency authorization was oral.
verification_notes: 21 CFR 1306.11(d)(2), (d)(4) and (d)(5) read verbatim in the current eCFR text on 2026-09-10. Added because the GPT-FRESH-B4-SG-REPAIR-V3 audit found the emergency oral record requirements absent and the DEA-notification consequence omitted, and FED-CII-EMERGENCY-FOLLOWUP and FED-CII-EMERGENCY-MISSING-FOLLOWUP are both frozen by MA-Q-0104's RELEASED adjudication.
